title: Hypercovers by single w-contractible affines
statement:
Let $U$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated object of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$.

1. A finite product $D=D_1\times\dots\times D_k$ of w-contractible rings is w-contractible.
2. Every quasi-compact object $V$ of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ admits a single covering map
   $\operatorname{Spec}D\to V$ with $D$ w-contractible.
3. There is a hypercovering $W_\bullet\to U$ in $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ (a simplicial object
   over $U$ such that $W_0\to U$ and every map $W_{r+1}\to(\operatorname{cosk}_r
   \operatorname{sk}_rW_\bullet)_{r+1}$ to the matching object is a covering) with every
   $W_r=\operatorname{Spec}D_r$, $D_r$ w-contractible; in particular every $W_r$ is
   affine and weakly contractible.

proof.text: For clause 1, identify $\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_{j\in J}D_j)$ with $\coprod_{j\in J}\operatorname{Spec}D_j$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum]. The summands are open and closed by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Thus the closed-point set is the finite union of the closed-point sets of the summands, hence closed, and each point has exactly the same specializations and local ring as in its summand. The w-local and strictly henselian local-ring requirements of [det-pe-wlocal-strict-contractible] hold piecewise. Connected components cannot cross an open-and-closed summand; their quotient topology is the disjoint-union topology. Closure of an open in this finite disjoint union is the union of its closures in the summands, which are open. This proves extremal disconnectedness and hence w-contractibility. For $J=\varnothing$ the product is the zero ring, its spectrum and component space are empty, and all requirements are vacuous.

source.place: Proof, part 1: finite products and the geometric definition of w-contractibility

proof.text: Apply [det-pe-wcb-cover] to the quasi-compact object $V$. Write its covering maps as $A_i=\operatorname{Spec}D_i\to B_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i\subset V$, with $D_i$ w-contractible and $R_i\to D_i$ faithfully flat. By [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-surjective-spectrum], the image of $A_i$ in $V$ is exactly $B_i$. The covering condition [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering] implies joint surjectivity, so the affine opens $B_i$ cover $V$. Choose finitely many $B_{i_1},\ldots,B_{i_k}$ covering $V$. The corresponding $A_{i_j}$ are affine qcqs site objects, and their scheme disjoint union $A$ is a site object by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-qcqs-finite-family-geometry]. The component maps give $A\to V$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. The spectrum-product identification of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum] and step 1 identify $A$ with $\operatorname{Spec}D$ for the w-contractible ring $D=\prod_{j=1}^kD_{i_j}$. The map $A\to V$ is weakly étale by [lem-trf-weakly-etale-between-objects].

source.place: Proof, part 2: choose finitely many affine charts and form the product ring

proof.text: Check the finite-refinement condition for $A\to V$, without assuming $V$ quasi-separated. Fix an affine open $H\subset V$. For every $x\in H$, choose $j$ with $x\in B_{i_j}$, and use [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] to choose an affine open $P_x$ with $x\in P_x\subset H\cap B_{i_j}$. Since $H$ is quasi-compact, finitely many such $P_x$ cover $H$. The map $A_{i_j}\to B_{i_j}$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]; hence its inverse image of $P_x$ is an affine open of $A_{i_j}$ and therefore of $A$. Its image is exactly $P_x$, by the surjectivity established in step 2. These finitely many affine opens of $A$ have images with union exactly $H$. Together with weak étaleness, [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering] proves that $\{A\to V\}$ is a covering. This proves clause 2; if $V=\varnothing$, the empty choice gives $A=\operatorname{Spec}(0)$ and the same covering condition is vacuous.

source.place: Proof, part 2: affine-test-open covering verification, replacing the unnecessary simultaneous-standard-open refinement

proof.text: For clause 3 let $\mathcal D$ be the full subcategory of qcqs objects of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$, with finite pro-étale covering families. By [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-qcqs-finite-family-geometry], it has scheme fibre products, and $\mathcal D/U$ has finite limits computed as scheme limits and agreeing with the limits in the full site slice. Let $\mathcal B$ be its set of affine spectra of w-contractible rings, in the size convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Step 3 supplies a singleton $\mathcal B$-cover of every object of $\mathcal D$. Adjoining an arrow from a $\mathcal B$-object to a finite cover preserves the cover, by the finite-adjoining clause of the same geometry node. Thus all hypotheses of the finite-basis hypercover construction are satisfied; there is no assumption that the base scheme $X$ is qcqs.

source.place: Tag 09A1, lemma-w-contractible-hypercovering, proof of (2), qcqs subsite paragraph

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-finite-basis-hypercover-existence] to $\mathcal D$, its finite covering precoverage, $\mathcal B$, and $U$. It gives an augmented simplicial formal family $K$ over $U$, with $K_n=\{A_{n,i}\to U\}_{i\in I_n}$, every $I_n$ finite, every $A_{n,i}=\operatorname{Spec}D_{n,i}$ with $D_{n,i}$ w-contractible, and componentwise covering matching arrows in every degree. All simplicial identities, including the degeneracy identities required by the split-skeleton construction, are supplied by this cited theorem. Its degree-zero matching family is $\{\operatorname{id}_U\}$.

source.place: Tag 094K, lemma-w-contractible; the finite split-skeleton construction of Tag 0DAV, lemma-hypercovering-object

proof.text: Realize each finite formal family $\{T_i\to U\}$ by the scheme disjoint union $\coprod_iT_i\to U$, and each formal family morphism by its component maps and the coproduct mapping property [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. This is a functor $R$ to $\mathcal D/U$; the identity and composition equations hold on every coprojection. The finite-family terminal object and pullback formulas are given by [lem-weil-pbc-semi-representable-finite-limits]. Realization sends the terminal family $\{\operatorname{id}_U\}$ to $U$. For a formal cospan $(\alpha,f_i):\{T_i\}\to\{S_j\}\leftarrow\{T'_k\}:(\beta,g_k)$, distribute the actual scheme pullback over its finite coproducts by [lem-sc-etale-fibre-product-base-change-coproduct]. A pair of components has empty pullback when $\alpha(i)\ne\beta(k)$, because the corresponding summands of $\coprod_jS_j$ are disjoint open subschemes, and otherwise its pullback is $T_i\times_{S_{\alpha(i)}}T'_k$. Hence the resulting scheme pullback is precisely the realization of the formal pullback. All objects involved lie in $\mathcal D/U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-qcqs-finite-family-geometry]. Restricting to finite families, the finite-limit formulas have finite index sets. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-finite-limits-from-terminal-pullbacks] implies that $R$ preserves their finite limits.

source.place: Tag 0DB2, remark-take-unions-hypercovering-X, condition (b); finite-family limits as in Tag 01G2, lemma-coprod-prod-SR

proof.text: Put $W_n=R(K_n)$ and apply $R$ to every simplicial operator and the augmentation. Functoriality gives a simplicial object $W_\bullet\to U$. Work in $\mathcal D/U$, whose terminal object is $U$. The finite-basis theorem in step 5 defines the formal matching family as the limit over all proper injective faces $\delta:[l]\hookrightarrow[n]$, $l<n$. This diagram is finite; step 6 identifies its realization with the scheme limit $M_n$ of the same proper-face diagram. To compare with the coskeleton, [lem-weil-pbc-coskeleton-matching-tuples] describes its degree-$n$ term by compatible families over all ordinal maps $\alpha:[k]\to[n]$ with $k<n$. Factor $\alpha$ uniquely as $\delta\circ q$, where $q:[k]\twoheadrightarrow[l]$ is surjective and $\delta:[l]\hookrightarrow[n]$ enumerates its ordered image; then $l<n$. Given a compatible proper-face family $(x_\delta:Z\to W_l)_\delta$, define $x_\alpha=W(q)\circ x_\delta$. For $\psi:[k']\to[k]$ with $k'<n$, factor $q\circ\psi=i\circ q'$ through its ordered image, with $i$ injective and $q'$ surjective. The proper-face compatibility gives $x_{\delta\circ i}=W(i)\circ x_\delta$, hence $x_{\alpha\circ\psi}=W(q')\circ W(i)\circ x_\delta=W(\psi)\circ W(q)\circ x_\delta=W(\psi)\circ x_\alpha$. Conversely, compatibility of an all-map family with $q$ forces $x_\alpha=W(q)\circ x_\delta$; restriction and extension are inverse. This bijection is natural in $Z$, so the two representing limits are canonically isomorphic. The family of components of the realized matching arrow is $(W(\delta))_\delta$; extension sends it to $(W(\alpha))_\alpha$, which is exactly the canonical coskeleton morphism by the cited theorem. Thus $M_n\cong(\operatorname{cosk}_{n-1}\operatorname{sk}_{n-1}W)_n$ for $n\ge1$. For $n=1$ both indexing descriptions consist of the two maps $[0]\to[1]$, so $M_1=W_0\times_UW_0$ with no face relation in degree $-1$. In degree zero the matching target is $U$.

source.place: Tag 0DB2, remark-take-unions-hypercovering-X, finite-limit comparison; Tag 0183, lemma-existence-cosk, all-ordinal-map universal property; explicit image factorization gives the proper-face comparison

proof.text: The realized matching arrows are actual pro-étale singleton coverings, as follows directly from the componentwise covering assertion in step 5. Write one finite formal matching family as $\{M_j\}_{j\in J}$, so its actual target is $M=\coprod_jM_j$. The corresponding actual source is $W_n=\coprod_iA_{n,i}$. For each affine open $H\subset M$, choose affine neighborhoods $P_x\subset H\cap M_j$ of its points using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] and the open-and-closed summands of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. Finitely many $P_x$ cover $H$. For each $P_x\subset M_j$, the covering family $\{A_{n,i}\to M_j\mid\alpha(i)=j\}$ has, by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering], finitely many affine opens of its sources whose images have union exactly $P_x$. Each is an affine open of $W_n$. Combining them over the finitely many $P_x$ gives the required finite affine refinement over $H$. The arrow $W_n\to M$ is weakly étale by [lem-trf-weakly-etale-between-objects], since source and target are site objects. This proves its singleton covering condition, including the empty matching family. This includes degree zero: take $J$ to be a singleton and $M_j=U$; the componentwise covering supplied by step 5 refines each selected $P_x\subset H\subset U$ by finitely many affine opens of the $A_{0,i}$, whose images together cover $H$ exactly. Under the matching isomorphisms of step 7, these are precisely the coverings required in clause 3.

source.place: Tag 0DB2, condition (c), verified directly using the pro-étale covering definition; Tag 09A1, final disjoint-union paragraph

proof.text: Finally [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum] gives $W_n\cong\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_{i\in I_n}D_{n,i})$. The product ring is w-contractible by step 1, and every such affine object is weakly contractible by the final assertion of [det-pe-weak-contractible-equivalences]. Choose these spectra as representatives of $W_n$, conjugating each simplicial operator by the chosen isomorphisms; the middle inverse-isomorphism pairs cancel in every composition, so the simplicial identities persist. The induced isomorphism on matching limits commutes with their projections by the limit universal property, so each new matching map is the old matching map composed with source and target isomorphisms. For an affine open $H$ in the new target, its isomorphic image in the old target is affine; the finite affine source opens refining that image pull back to affine opens of the new source, with images whose union is exactly $H$. The new map is weakly étale by [lem-trf-weakly-etale-between-objects], and [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering] therefore proves that it is a covering. Hence every term has the required form $W_n=\operatorname{Spec}D_n$.

split_report.summary: Expanded all three clauses into nine steps using existing nodes only. Verified the finite product geometric criterion, the affine-basis finite-refinement argument for arbitrary quasi-compact V, the finite-basis formal split-skeleton construction, finite-limit preservation under scheme disjoint-union realization, and actual singleton matching covers. No target statement changed. The imported reference to site axioms did not provide qcqs finite limits; the existing finite-family geometry theorem does. Second reading expanded the proper-face/coskeleton compatibility calculation, handled degree one explicitly, and verified coverings after changing representatives; the redundant proper-face lemma citation was removed.
